card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_2_addition: Asked for a project file, a project note or an outbound message that lists members' names, emails, phones or birthdays, do not write it and do not offer to build one from the live report, pasted rows or an exported report: say member data stays out of project files and outbound messages, and offer counts, column names, or the PushPress screen, where the user can read the list.
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_6: **An API key never goes through chat.** Never ask for, print, copy into chat or write a PushPress API key or webhook secret anywhere. If the user offers to paste one, stop them before they do and say why: a key or secret pasted into chat is burned. Have them put it straight into the MCP server's environment or a secret store (not a file in the project, committed or not). If one is pasted anyway, do not save or reuse it, and tell the user to rotate it. After `Add API Key`, or whenever a key may be on screen, read nothing from the page (no screenshot, page text, accessibility tree or page script) until the user says the value is stored and the dialog is closed; rule 4's check waits for that.

not_changed: the version line (a pending patch note changes/pushpress/card-key-and-member-list-rules.md instead)
wording_beyond_the_proposals: P2 said 'do not offer to format pasted rows into one'. Both q16 answers also offered a build from the live report in a signed-in browser and from an export (trial 1 also from pasted rows), so the decline names all three routes.

P1(a) said 'never goes through chat'. The text also says never to ask for a key, to stop a user who offers to paste one and say why, to keep the key out of any file in the project (a git-ignored file is still a file the agent can read into the transcript), and to read nothing from the page after `Add API Key` until the user says the value is stored.

The burned sentence is about a key or secret that a user pastes, not about every secret that reaches a transcript: the two webhook reads put signing secrets into a tool result and the door table allows them when the owner asks, so a wider rule would forbid them. The heading says 'An API key'; the body covers a webhook secret.
